likely_cause.reasoning: Inference. The registration was not lost or re-created: RDAP shows a creation date of 2010-12-07, an expiry of 2030-12-07, client delete/renew/transfer/update locks, registrar GoDaddy, and GoDaddy nameservers (ns23/ns24.domaincontrol.com), so this is not a lapsed-then-reregistered domain. An Internet Archive capture of the same URL from 2026-04-20 still shows the genuine roofing site (title about a local NJ roofing company, 30+ years), so the replacement happened between April 2026 and today. The domain now resolves to 160.153.0.162, hostname 162.0.153.160.host.secureserver.net (GoDaddy shared hosting), which is consistent with the site's files being replaced inside a hosting account rather than the name being moved to a third-party spam host. That points to a compromised or unauthorised change to the site/hosting content; only the owner's registrar and hosting account logs can confirm how access was obtained. An abandoned or parked-with-monetisation explanation cannot be fully excluded from public data.

fix_steps.step: Confirm who holds the GoDaddy account for biondoroofing.com, that the domain is set to auto-renew, and that two-step verification is on. The domain is already paid to 7 Dec 2030, so the fix is about account access, not renewal.
fix_steps.who: Owner plus whoever originally set up the website or domain

fix_steps.step: Inside the GoDaddy hosting account, find and remove the gambling page, restore the site from the most recent clean backup, then change the hosting, WordPress (if used) and email passwords. If no clean backup exists, keep the domain serving a holding page until a replacement is ready.
fix_steps.who: Web developer, with the owner on the account

fix_steps.step: Publish a simple one-page site at the domain straight away: company name, services, towns served, phone, licence number and a few job photos. A static page or page-builder template keeps it from being overwritten again.

Repair the places customers are sent: edit the website field on the Google Business Profile so it points to a working page, and update or remove the old link on the AECinfo, FindTrustedRoofers, Houzz and the biondo-contracting.webflow.io entries (plus BBB, which we could not open).
fix_steps.who: Owner or office manager; developer for the directory edits

fix_steps.step: Once the spam is gone, use Google's removals tool for the domain in Search Console to block the old URL from results, request a refresh of outdated content, and add uptime plus content-change monitoring so a repeat replacement is noticed within a day.

after_fix.opportunity: Add an online quote request (with roof-photo upload) and a tap-to-call button, linked from the Google profile, so enquiries stop depending on a phone call.
after_fix.evidence: The Google Business Profile offers an address, hours and the phone number (732) 257-2926, with the website field pointing at the broken domain; no listing page we opened offers a form or booking, while the profile's 4.9 rating and review volume (172 reviews on Birdeye) show steady demand.

# Website Health Check: Biondo Contracting

## What we saw on 13 November 2026

- biondoroofing.com, the site on your Google Business Profile, still loads but shows a Thai-language slot/gambling page styled as a Google Play listing; there is no roofing content (screenshots kept).
- The profile "Biondo Contracting-Roofing Specialists" (4.9, 38 Spotswood Ave, Monroe Township, (732) 257-2926) still uses that domain as its website link.
- The domain has not lapsed: the registry shows it created in 2010, paid to 7 December 2030, with GoDaddy locks in place, and an Internet Archive capture from 20 April 2026 still shows your roofing site.
- AECinfo and FindTrustedRoofers still publish the domain, and a small Webflow page headed "Biondoroofing.com" links to it.

## What it means for customers

A homeowner who taps the website on your profile lands on a gambling page and finds no services, towns served or way to ask for a quote. The phone number still works, so enquiries depend on someone calling.

## How to fix it

1. Confirm who holds the GoDaddy account and turn on two-step verification (owner and site builder, 0.5-1 hour).
2. Remove the injected page in the hosting account, restore the last clean backup, change hosting and site passwords (developer, 1-3 hours).
3. Publish a simple one-page site: services, towns, phone, licence number, photos (developer, 2-4 hours).
4. Update the website field on Google plus the AECinfo, FindTrustedRoofers, Houzz and Webflow links (owner, 1-2 hours).
5. Ask Google to refresh the removed page in results and set up change monitoring (developer, 1-2 hours).

## After the fix

Add an online quote request with roof-photo upload and tap-to-call, linked from the profile; enquiries would no longer depend on a phone call.

Prepared from publicly available information on 13 November 2026. We did not log in to or change anything.
